notes:
Built-in `/code-review` (medium, `HEAD~1...HEAD`) returned 6 findings, all rejected. They cite `packages/runtime/src/instructions/...` (design.md, web-design, core.md, requirements.md), which this commit does not touch (`git diff --stat HEAD~1 HEAD -- packages/runtime/src/instructions` is empty). The skill most likely ran against the shared tree, not this worktree. Treat it as a mis-targeted run, not a review of this change.
Non-blocking, `packages/runtime/src/cli/status.ts` ~L36-41: the skip rule tests only that the first move leaves a full commit id and that the second move leaves that move's destination. It never checks that the destination is the default branch, although the doc comment says so.
  - A cloud session that starts detached, goes to some branch `B`, then to branch `C` would now report `C`; the old code reported `B`.
  - It is indistinguishable from the platform flow, so I would not block. Checking `origin/HEAD` would tighten it.
Cases that behave as before: a clone with no moves, a clone followed by user switches (first source is a branch name), a short reflog (one move, so no skip), and a platform session already on `main`.
Expired reflog: the clone and detach entries are the oldest, so they expire first. The assigned-branch move survives and still resolves correctly.
If the assigned branch was later deleted, the loop falls back to the source `main`, which is the old behavior.
The `safeBranch` allowlist, `check-ref-format` and the `show-ref` existence check still apply to the chosen name through `returnBranch` (unchanged).
The dist bundles match the source change (Claude bundle diff inspected; Pi not read). Reading only: I did not run the real claude.ai flow.
